newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico accuses servants of multiple homicide.
newsitem.headline: Mexico accuses servants of multiple homicide.

text.p: A family of five who were murdered in their beds in early December in a crime that stunned Mexico were bludgeoned to death by their servants, Mexico City authorities alleged on Monday.

Many had speculated that the family was murdered in a drug hit, or because the parents -- author Yolanda Figueroa and her husband, former anti-drugs agent Fernando Balderas -- had blamed government corruption for delaying the arrest of a top drug lord.

But the Mexico City attorney general's office said on Monday two of the family's chauffeurs had murdered the family in revenge because Balderas had raped one of their wives and tried to rape the wife of the other. Both women were maids in the household.

Gen. Luis Gutierrez, director of the Judicial Police in Mexico City, told Television Azteca one of the chauffeurs who had to be put in a hospital with head injuries after the attack had confessed to murdering the family with the help of his fellow driver and the two wives. Gutierrez did not say how the chauffeur was injured.
The wife and three children, age 18, 14 and 9, were beaten to death with an iron rod after the alleged murderers killed Balderas and then lost control, Gutierrez said.
The second chauffeur and his wife had fled after the attack and were wanted by police, Gutierrez said.

In a book published in August, Figueroa alleged that the government had all the elements it needed to capture jailed cocaine kingpin Juan Garcia Abrego nearly three years before his arrest in January 1996 -- raising speculation that drugs or politics may have been the motive for the family's murder.
Her book relied largely on information from Balderas, who was a key adviser in the attorney general's office in the early 1990s.
